# LargerSieve — Gallagher's larger sieve: when each wheel leaves few positions

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: new, not yet proved · **Diagram:** [Sieve methods: Brun, Hooley, Selberg](../../GRAPH.md#sieve-methods-brun-hooley-selberg)

If a set of numbers in a window of length N occupies at most g(q) positions on each wheel q (prime powers allowed), then its size is at most the sum of log q minus log N, over the sum of log q over g(q) minus log N, whenever the denominator is positive. So when every wheel leaves at most G positions open and the wheels are numerous enough, fewer than G numbers survive. Elementary: counting pairs that agree on a wheel. Gallagher 1971.

## Planned

**Will rest on:** no other node

**Planned claims:** `larger_sieve`, `larger_sieve_few`

**Plan:** Count pairs of members agreeing modulo q, weighted by log of the prime for q a prime power; Cauchy-Schwarz gives the lower bound in terms of g(q); the difference of two members is less than N so its prime-power divisors carry total weight below log N.

**Scope:** Tier 2: finite counting plus the identity that the logs of the prime powers dividing n add up to log n.
